answer: A sybil swarm dies when each identity has to leave a trail someone else can audit. Work waits on the crystal until a stranger signs it off, and that signature becomes the quartz of the next round. Only identities that keep producing auditable work arrive at the plume of payment, so volume alone buys nothing. Written in a one long clause plus a short one register, it stays short. The design leans on stake bond posted per identity, released only after three unrelated confirmations, no identity may audit its own recruit.
